title: Invertibility of the internal-Hom counit composite
statement: Let C,D be monoidal categories, H:Cᵒᵖ×C→C and J:Dᵒᵖ×D→D bifunctors, F:C→D and R:D→C with adjunction a:F⊣R. Suppose tensor-right by K is left adjoint to H(K,-) on C and J(K,-) on D, with specified adjunctions bC,bD. Let t:F(- tensor -)≅F(-) tensor F(-) be a natural isomorphism and gamma:H→R J(F(-),F(-)) a natural transformation whose adjunct at (K,L) is the bD transpose of t.inv at (H(K,L),K) followed by F of bC(K).counit at L. Then for every M in C and E in D, gamma(M,R(E)) followed by R J(1,a.counit(E)) is an isomorphism.

source.place: Remark 08I3 (cohomology-remark-prepare-fancy-base-change) with Tag 079W and Lemma 08DJ (cohomology-lemma-internal-hom); standard internal form of the Lf^* -| Rf_* adjunction (Lipman, Notes on derived functors, Prop. 3.2.3)

proof.text: For every test object A, define e1 as inverse tensor-Hom adjunction on C, inverse pullback adjunction, and precomposition with t.inv; define e2 as inverse pullback adjunction followed by inverse tensor-Hom adjunction on D. Naturality of the adjunction hom equivalences, the mate hypothesis and naturality of t.inv prove e2(q followed by c)=e1(q). Thus postcomposition by c equals e1 followed by e2 inverse and is bijective. Apply Mathlib isIso_of_yoneda_map_bijective.

theorem internalHomCounitMate_isIso
    {C : Type uC} {D : Type uD} [Category.{vC} C] [Category.{vD} D]
    [MonoidalCategory C] [MonoidalCategory D]
    (H : Cᵒᵖ × C ⥤ C) (J : Dᵒᵖ × D ⥤ D)
    (F : C ⥤ D) (R : D ⥤ C) (a : F ⊣ R)
    (bC : ∀ K : C, tensorRight K ⊣ (Functor.curry.obj H).obj (op K))
    (bD : ∀ K : D, tensorRight K ⊣ (Functor.curry.obj J).obj (op K))
    (t : tensor C ⋙ F ≅ F.prod F ⋙ tensor D)
    (γ : H ⟶ F.op.prod F ⋙ J ⋙ R)
    (hγ : ∀ K L : C,
      (a.homEquiv (H.obj (op K, L)) (J.obj (op (F.obj K), F.obj L))).symm
        (γ.app (op K, L)) =
      (bD (F.obj K)).homEquiv (F.obj (H.obj (op K, L))) (F.obj L)
        (t.inv.app (H.obj (op K, L), K) ≫ F.map ((bC K).counit.app L)))
    (M : C) (E : D) :
    IsIso (γ.app (op M, R.obj E) ≫
      R.map (J.map (X := (op (F.obj M), F.obj (R.obj E)))
        (Y := (op (F.obj M), E)) ((𝟙 (F.obj M)).op, a.counit.app E)))
